samples.summary: Hand-rolled SQL literal escaping reinvents `mysql2`'s own escaper, which is already imported in this file
samples.evidence: `import * as mysql from 'mysql2/promise'` is already present (line 3), and mysql2 re-exports SqlString's `escape`/`format` (also available as `pool.escape()`). The delta grows a bespoke `sql()` helper (`value.replace(/\\/g,'\\\\').replace(/'/g,"''")`) plus a paragraph of dialect commentary and dedicated unit tests to re-derive escaping rules the dependency already implements correctly and completely (it also handles \0, \n, \r, \x1a and "). The repo's stated norm is reuse over re-implementation; the fact that this round had to add a backslash case after shipping a quote-only version is exactly the maintenance cost that reuse avoids. `mysql.escape(value)` (or `mysql.format('… document_id = ?', [id])` for the whole predicate) gives the same string-interpolation-without-prepared-statements approach the design doc prescribes, with no bespoke escaper to keep in sync.

samples.summary: Design doc still asserts only server-derived ids are interpolated, while the delta hardens `sql()` against adversarial values
samples.evidence: docs/design/share-link-analytics.md:149-152 and its Risks section (line 334-336) state the mitigation as "interpolating only server-derived ids and server-validated date ranges; never interpolate raw client input". The new tests and comment treat `documentId` as attacker-controlled and escape it defensively. The canonical doc is not updated to record the actual escaping contract (backslash + quote doubling) that the code now relies on, so the doc and code describe different threat models.

samples.summary: 403-specific messaging added/tested only for the document dashboard; the workspace analytics page keeps the generic text with no shared error component
samples.evidence: document-analytics.tsx:59-69 special-cases HttpError 403 and the new test locks that in, while workspace-analytics.tsx:39 still renders the generic `Failed to load analytics.` for every error. If issue #732's outcome covers the analytics dashboards generally, the workspace page is uncovered; either way the two pages now duplicate hand-rolled error-state markup instead of sharing one helper.
